Koo Bon-hyun, a nephew of the late LG Group honorary chairman Koo Cha-kyung, was detained upon arriving in the country Monday to undergo an investigation on suspicion of violating the Capital Markets Act, embezzlement and breach of trust, according to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. The 57-year-old left for the Netherlands in 2018 amid suspicions that he made illegal profits of 14.5 billion won ($10.9 million) by disclosing false information about a KOSDAQ-listed company he had acquired without capital. He is also accused of embezzling 4.6 billion won from the firm, including for entertainment expenses. Police obtained a detention warrant for Koo in 2019 and requested that Interpol issue a Red Notice for him. Cambodian police apprehended him in September and repatriated him back to Korea this week. items.title: 'Soju should not exist': Surgeon warns of addiction risk from cheap, strong alcohol
items.title_zh: “烧酒不该存在”：外科医生警告廉价烈酒的成瘾风险
items.summary: Click here for more articles by Kormedi.com. A practicing surgeon has issued a strong warning about the dangers of soju — a popular traditional Korean alcohol that is now mass manufactured — drawing on his own experience of severe alcohol addiction. Lee Jun-suh, a hepatopancreatobiliary surgeon, appeared on the YouTube channel Doctor Dinho on Tuesday and said, "Soju is a drink that should not exist." "Its alcohol content is far too high for its price, fueling alcohol addiction," he said. Gastroenterologist Kim Tae-kyun agreed, saying, "At that price and concentration, shouldn't soju be considered a drug rather than an alcoholic beverage?" Lee said, "Alcoholic drinks like this type of diluted soju are uncommon. The availability of soju makes it far too easy for people to drink alcohol." Lee, who has overcome alcohol addiction, said he once underestimated the severity of his own dependence even while treating patients with end-stage liver and pancreatic diseases. items.title: Korea urges Japan to face full history of Sado mine during separate memorial
items.title_zh: 韩国在单独举行的纪念活动上敦促日本正视佐渡矿山的全部历史
items.summary: Korea on Friday called on Japan to fully acknowledge the history of wartime forced labor at the Sado mine complex as it held a separate memorial ceremony for Korean victims of forced labor for the third consecutive year. Korean Ambassador to Japan Lee Hyuk made the call during the ceremony held at a hotel on Sado Island in Niigata Prefecture, with nine family members of the victims attending. "Many Korean workers had been mobilized against their will and forced to work at the mine through government-arranged labor placement and conscription under the involvement of the Japanese colonial government-general," Lee said in his memorial address. "Remembering the pain of the past and sharing our condolences here today will deepen our sense of empathy and healing, and provide an opportunity for everyone to fully understand the entire history of the Sado mine as a World Heritage site," he added. More than 1,500 Koreans were mobilized to work at the Sado mine during Japan's 1910-45 colonial rule of Korea. items.title: Remains of 2 Korean independence fighters to return home from US, Uzbekistan

items.summary: The remains of two Korean independence fighters laid to rest in the United States and Uzbekistan will return home next week to mark the 80th anniversary of a project to repatriate the remains of such activists from overseas, the veterans ministry said Friday. The remains of Ho Si-han and Lee Gwal will be brought back from the U.S. and Uzbekistan, respectively, on Sunday, according to the ministry. It marks the first time that the remains of an independence fighter buried in Uzbekistan will return home. An event marking their return will be held at a memorial park in Seoul on Monday, attended by some 300 personnel, and the remains will later be buried at the national cemetery in the central city of Daejeon. Ho, born in Seoul in 1885, was arrested by the Japanese police while raising military funds following the March 1 independence movement against Japan's 1910-45 colonial rule of Korea. He also took part in a number of fundraising schemes to support the Korean independence movement from 1927 to 1945, before he died in Los Angeles in 1956. items.title: Korea's rice production falls for 5th year in 2026 amid changing diets
items.title_zh: 随着饮食习惯的改变，韩国水稻产量在2026年将连续第五年下降
items.summary: Korea's rice output declined for the fifth consecutive year in 2026 amid changing dietary habits, data showed Friday, with the cultivation area also reaching a new low. Rice production decreased 0.9 percent year-on-year to 3.5 million tons this year, according to data compiled by the Ministry of Data and Statistics. It marked the fourth-lowest level since the government began compiling the data in 1965. The combined area of rice paddies in the country fell 1.1 percent year-on-year to 670,000 hectares, the smallest on record. Despite the decline in overall production, output per 1,000 square meters increased 0.2 percent year-on-year to 524 kilograms this year, according to the ministry. Rice remains a staple food in Korea, but consumption has steadily fallen in recent decades amid shifts in dietary preferences. The decrease in production also came amid the government's efforts to manage output while encouraging farmers to switch to other crops. items.title: Defense ministry conducting poll on military cadets over proposed academy integration

items.summary: The defense ministry said Friday it is surveying military cadets on the proposal to integrate the Army, Air Force and Navy academies as the government seeks to revise the plan amid pushback from alumni groups and key stakeholders. The online survey, running from Friday through Tuesday, will poll 2,350 cadets across all four class years, excluding about 143 naval cadets set to be deployed for rotational training, a ministry official told reporters. The ministry is pushing to merge the three institutions into a unified military academy, but the plan has drawn fierce opposition from cadets and alumni who say it could erode the distinct identity and specialized capabilities of each armed service. The ministry is now reportedly weighing the option of relocating the military academy of the Army out of Seoul as planned while retaining the two others, a move seen as backtracking from its original merger plan. Oh will formally take office on Monday to lead the agency, which is affiliated with the foreign ministry and responsible for the government's official development assistance (ODA) programs. After entering the foreign service in 1994, Oh held various posts in development cooperation and multilateral diplomacy, including deputy chief of mission at South Korea's U.N. mission. She became South Korea's first female ambassador to the Holy See in January 2023 and was appointed third deputy director of the National Security Office in June last year. "Oh is expected to actively realize KOICA's vision of becoming a leading global development cooperation agency that pursues universal values and shared national interests, while strengthening its role as an integrated platform for South Korea's grant aid programs," the ministry said in a statement. items.title: Lee pledges capital market reform to address stock undervaluation

Lee made the pledge during a policy discussion on the capital market held at the Korea Exchange, which brought together experts, corporate representatives and government officials. The president described the undervaluation of Korean stocks as an "unreasonable abnormality," reaffirming his administration's commitment to reforming the capital market and the broader financial market to boost investor confidence. Lee's remarks came amid significant volatility in Korea's stock market in recent months, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) trading in the mid-5,000-point range on Friday, after reaching an all-time closing high of 9,114.55 points in late June. items.title: Gov't vows zero tolerance against cheating with AI glasses

The suspicions emerged following revelations that the highest scorer in the tax accountant exam received a near-perfect score, missing only one question out of the 160 on the first-round test, earning 397.5 points out of a possible 400, a score many test-takers view as unrealistic. That has raised concerns that AI cheating can be used in the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), set for Thursday. "The government views cheating using AI smart glasses as a serious issue that infringes upon fair opportunities for students who have worked diligently, and takes people's concerns regarding this matter very seriously," the Office for Government Policy Coordination said in a statement. items.title: Lee's approval rating falls back below 40%: poll
items.title_zh: 民调：李家超的支持率回落至40%以下
items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating slipped back to 39 percent this week, a weekly poll showed Friday, amid negative sentiment over his real estate policies and economic concerns. The survey, conducted by Gallup Korea from Tuesday through Thursday on 1,002 people aged 18 and older, showed that positive assessments of Lee's performance fell 2 percentage points from the previous week, when the figure stood at 41 percent. Lee's approval rating has fluctuated around the 40 percent mark in recent weeks after hitting a low of 37 percent in October. Those who disapproved of Lee's handling of state affairs remained unchanged from the previous week at 50 percent. Real estate policies were cited the most by those who disapproved of Lee's performance at 17 percent, followed by economic and livelihood concerns at 15 percent. Among those who positively assessed Lee's performance, 19 percent cited economic and livelihood issues, followed by diplomacy at 17 percent and communication at 9 percent. items.title: Saudi, Chinese officials discuss Houthi attacks, regional security and maritime navigation

items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan met with Chinese Special Envoy for Middle East Affairs Zhai Jun to discuss bilateral relations and ongoing Houthi attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Kingdom. During the meeting, the two officials reviewed Saudi-Chinese relations and the implications of the Houthi attacks for regional security and stability. They also discussed regional developments and diplomatic efforts to contain crises and de-escalate tensions. Both sides stressed the importance of strengthening energy security, maintaining market stability and safeguarding maritime corridors and freedom of navigation, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait, to ensure the smooth flow of global trade and supply chains. The meeting was attended by Undersecretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Political Affairs Dr. Saud Al-Sati.

items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯对阿联酋富查伊拉港致命事件表示声援
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia has expressed its solidarity with the United Arab Emirates following an incident at the Port of Fujairah that resulted in deaths and injuries. In a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday, Saudi Arabia expressed its sincere condolences and sympathy to the UAE’s leadership, government and people, as well as the families of the victims. The Kingdom also wished those injured in the incident a speedy recovery.

items.title: Coalition intercepts drones in Riyadh and eastern regions
items.title_zh: 联军在利雅得和东部地区拦截无人机
items.summary: RIYADH — Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, stated that a drone, fired by the terrorist Houthi militia, was intercepted and destroyed in the Riyadh region. He said that another drone was intercepted and destroyed in the Eastern Province.

items.title: Saudi-US business ties gain momentum with landmark cooperation agreement
items.title_zh: 沙特与美国的商业关系因具有里程碑意义的合作协议而势头强劲
items.summary: WASHINGTON — The US-Saudi Business Council and the Federation of Saudi Chambers have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen ties between the business communities of Saudi Arabia and the United States of America. The agreement was signed by the Council’s Chairman and CEO Charles Hallab and the Federation’s Secretary General Sultan Al-Musallam. The signing ceremony was attended by Assistant Secretary General for International Trade at the Federation of Saudi Chambers Majid Al-Mutairi and President of the Middle East sector at Mayer Brown Company Tom Thraya in Washington, D.C. The MoU establishes a framework for enhancing communication between companies in the two countries, developing investment opportunities, and addressing challenges facing businesses in both markets. The Federation of Saudi Chambers is playing a key role in the partnership as the representative body of the Saudi private sector, ensuring that the sector’s perspectives and needs are duly considered. The memorandum sets out practical mechanisms for cooperation between the council and the federation, including facilitating trade delegation visits and communication between business leaders, supporting investments and strategic partnerships, exchanging market information and expertise, and working through relevant channels to facilitate companies’ entry into both markets and address the obstacles they encounter. A joint working group will supervise the implementation of the memorandum and develop a joint action plan. Senior representatives from both sides will meet every three months to assess progress, identify priority sectors and activities, set timelines, and assign responsibilities. Speaking on the occasion, Hallab said that the Federation of Saudi Chambers is a key partner for the council in connecting with and supporting the Saudi private sector. “This agreement allows the Council and the Federation to bring companies together, work towards common goals, and strengthen trade relations between our two countries. We value the federation’s leadership and friendship, and we look forward to further developing this partnership,” he said. The memorandum also provides for cooperation in activating the federation’s “International Business Concierge” initiative, which seeks to facilitate international business and attract and facilitate US investments in the Kingdom. Other areas of collaboration include implementing sector-specific initiatives, organizing business-to-business meetings and engagements between businesses and government entities, and supporting Saudi exports to the US market. Established in 1993 through a Saudi Royal Decree and a US Executive Order, the Saudi-US Business Council is a leading bilateral business organization committed to expanding trade and investment and promoting commercial cooperation between Saudi Arabia and the United States. The Council brings together influential business and government leaders from both countries, providing a platform to identify priorities in bilateral trade relations, unlock transformative investment opportunities, and address key challenges affecting trade and business.

items.title: Crown Prince congratulates Grenada prime minister on his re-election
items.title_zh: 王储祝贺格林纳达总理再次当选
items.summary: RIYADH — Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman has sent a cable of congratulations to Prime Minister of Grenada Dickon Mitchel on the occasion of his re-election as prime minister.The Crown Prince expressed his sincere congratulations and best wishes for success to Mitchel, and for further progress and prosperity to the friendly people of Grenada.

items.title: Airbag defect hits 44,305 Hyundai Elantra vehicles; owners urged to get free repairs
items.title_zh: 44305辆现代伊兰特汽车出现安全气囊缺陷；车主被敦促进行免费维修
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Commerce has renewed its call for owners of Hyundai Elantra vehicles, manufactured between 2009 and 2011, to respond to recall campaigns over a defect in the driver's airbag inflator that could cause serious or fatal injuries.The ministry urged owners of the 44,305 affected vehicles remaining in Saudi Arabia to stop driving them immediately and contact authorized dealers to arrange free repairs to ensure their safety. The ministry explained that the previously announced recall covered 57,195 vehicles, of which approximately 12,890 have been repaired, representing 22 percent of the total. However, 44,305 vehicles remain unrepaired, underscoring the importance of promptly contacting authorized dealers across the Kingdom to address the defect.The ministry stressed the need for an immediate response to the recall. It urged owners to contact the authorized dealers: Wallan Company at 8001240401, Almajdouie Company at 8003040777, or Mohamed Yousuf Naghi & Brothers Group at 8001240191, to arrange the necessary repairs free of charge.

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Kenya sign deal to regulate recruitment of domestic workers
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯与肯尼亚签署协议，规范家政服务人员的招聘
items.summary: RIYADH — Deputy Minister of Human Resources and Social Development for Labor Abdullah Abuthnain received Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Labour and Social Protection Alfred Nganga Mutua at the ministry’s headquarters in Riyadh on Thursday. Several senior Saudi ministry officials and the accompanying Kenyan delegation also attended the meeting. The meeting discussed ways to strengthen cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Kenya in areas of mutual interest in the labor sector, particularly by developing cooperation mechanisms for the recruitment of domestic workers, improving the effectiveness of pre-departure training and qualification programs, and raising awareness of contractual rights and obligations. These efforts aimed to enhance the readiness of domestic workers, improve the quality of recruitment services, promote stability in contractual relations, and protect the rights of all parties. The two sides also discussed mechanisms for strengthening technical coordination, exchanging expertise and best practices in training and qualification, and improving procedures related to the recruitment of domestic workers. These measures aimed to enhance the efficiency of recruitment processes, improve their outcomes, and serve the mutual interests of both countries. Following the meeting, Abdullah Abuthnain and Alfred Nganga Mutua signed a technical annex to the agreement on the recruitment of domestic workers between Saudi Arabia and Kenya, signed on July 5, 2026. The annex is part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and develop the technical and regulatory mechanisms governing the recruitment of domestic workers. The technical annex aims to streamline procedures and reduce the costs of recruiting domestic workers from Kenya to Saudi Arabia. It also seeks to improve the efficiency of recruitment mechanisms, ensure compliance with approved regulations, protect the rights of employers and domestic workers, and regulate the contractual relationship between the two parties. The signing of the annex builds on the longstanding relations and ongoing cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Kenya, reflecting both sides’ commitment to developing their partnership in labor-related fields, improving the efficiency of the recruitment system, and promoting sustainable cooperation that serves the mutual interests of both countries.

items.title: 6 expat women arrested for prostitution in Eastern Province
items.title_zh: 6名外籍女性因卖淫在东部省被捕
items.summary: DAMMAM — The Eastern Province police, in coordination with the General Directorate for Community Security and Combating Human Trafficking, arrested six expatriate women on charges of prostitution. The operation comes as part of ongoing security efforts to monitor, detect, and apprehend violators and those involved in criminal activities. Public Security stated that the women were taken into custody and initial legal procedures were initiated against them, pending further legal action. The women were subsequently referred to the Public Prosecution to complete the necessary judicial procedures in accordance with applicable regulations. The arrests were part of the continuous security campaigns carried out by the relevant authorities to combat crimes against public morals and strengthen community security across the Kingdom.

items.title: Saudi schools to begin 10-day autumn holiday on Nov. 20
items.title_zh: 沙特学校将于11月20日开始为期10天的秋季假期
items.summary: RIYADH — Students in public schools across Saudi Arabia are eagerly anticipating an upcoming 10-day holiday in the 1448 AH academic calendar, comprising the autumn break and an additional one-day holiday. According to the academic calendar, the holiday will begin on Friday, November 20, 2026, and continue through Sunday, Nov. 29. The autumn break will run from Nov. 20 to 28, followed by an additional day off on Nov. 29. Students are scheduled to return to classrooms on Monday, Nov. 30, 2026, following the 10-day break, and resume their academic activities for the remainder of the semester.
